pitch: Watt the repair robot rolls home through twenty-three haywire circuit boards. Route the current, never touch it.

keys.R: Reboot the board (costs a spare battery)

news.head: Ohm Sweet Ohm: puzzles made of pure Game-Maker
news.html: A thunderstorm has scrambled the Bitmores' brand-new Smart Home, and Watt, the pocket-sized repair robot who lives in the fuse box, must roll home through twenty-three haywire circuit boards, from the toaster to the attic. Every switch, fuse and relay is built from ordinary Game-Maker blocks and monsters: batteries are blocks that give birth to "current" monsters, and gates fall when a stronger monster touches them. Not one line of code!

news.head: Since last issue: Two years of Sparky mail
news.html: It has been a while since issue 2, and the mailbag filled up. Your favorite gadget in In The Year 2000! was the Teleport-A-Phone. Your least favorite moment was running out of quarters at the Phone Exchange (every room has more, and they come back each time you dial). Three of you sent drawings of Sparky 3000, and one of you built him out of a shoebox and two flashlights.

news.head: Around the Sandbox: New address, new computer
news.html: Where did we go? The founder finished high school, a 486 with a CD-ROM drive turned up as a graduation present, and Sandbox Software moved to Pittsburgh, where the founder is studying at the Art Institute of Pittsburgh. You can see it on the boxes. The best part of the new desk is a modem: our own BBS is online at 1-412-555-SAND, and every Sandbox game, hint and high-score list goes there first.

news.head: In the workshop: Can Game-Maker scroll a shooter?
news.html: Everybody on the BBS says Game-Maker can't do a real scrolling shoot-'em-up. We think it can. The workbench has a nano-fighter, a lot of graph paper covered in circuit traces, and a title: Virus Blaster. A hint: it's set somewhere very close to you right now.

news.head: Letters: "Is the pocket telephone real?"
news.html:
"Dex's science report is about a telephone that fits in your pocket. Is that a real invention?" - A reader, by mail

The Scoop replies: Not yet. In our BBS poll it got two votes, and one of those was a joke. Ask us again in the year 2000.

items.title: Ohm Sweet Ohm Hint Book
items.note: A nudge and an answer for every board
items.intro: Stuck on a board? Find it below. The question tells you what most people get stuck on; the answer, printed under red, tells you how to get past. Read the answers through the red film, one at a time, and only when you need them! (Heard the felt-maker left something behind in the wiring? See the last page.)

hints.q: The Toaster: How do I get past the crackling gate?
hints.a: Bump the switch from below to turn it on. Current runs along the wire to the gate and shuts it down. Keep off the wire while it glows!

hints.q: The Blender: The gate is open, but the wire next to it is live!
hints.a: A gate stays open once current has reached it. Bump the switch again to turn the power off, wait for the last spark to drain away, then walk through.

hints.q: The Microwave: Two switches and one gate. Which one?
hints.a: Either switch opens the gate: two wires into one gate means either will do. The left switch puts live current right in front of the gate (turn it off again if you use it). The right one keeps its current inside the housing.

hints.q: The Dishwasher: The second switch fences me away from the second gate!
hints.a: Two gates, one after the other. Open the first with the switch at the top left. For the second, slip around behind its switch BEFORE you turn it on, and bump it from below: then the live wire is behind you.

hints.q: The Fridge: I rolled through the arrow and now I cannot get back to the switch.
hints.a: The arrow is a diode: you can only go through it the way it points. Before you go through, turn the switch on, wait for the gate to open, and turn the switch OFF again.

hints.q: The Coffee Maker: I turned the top switch on and now I am stuck down by the bottom switch!
hints.a: Two switches in a row both have to be on. Turn on the bottom one FIRST, while the wire is still dead, then the top one. When the gate opens, turn the top switch off again so you can step over the wire.

hints.q: The Doorbell: The button turns the current on, and then I am fenced out.
hints.a: It is a timer button: it turns the current off again by itself after a few seconds. Push it, watch the gate shut down, wait for the wire to go dark, then walk in. (Or push it from the inside!)

hints.q: The TV Set: If I turn the power on, I can never cross that wire. If I don't, the gate stays shut.
hints.a: That is a timer button, not a switch. Bump it as you go by: it turns itself off after about five seconds. Wait for the gate to open and the wire to go dark, then cross.

hints.q: The VCR: The current keeps coming and going. How do I get across?
hints.a: Those batteries pulse: on for a moment, off for a moment, and the two take turns. Wait next to a wire until the current has just gone by, then roll across. Stop between the two wires and do it again.

hints.q: The Floor Lamp: One wire is always live, and there is no switch for it!
hints.a: Bump a fuse and it blows for good, and its wire goes dead. Follow the copper: the LEFT fuse feeds the wire in front of the gate. Blow that one, never the right one (it feeds the gate). Then turn on the switch.

hints.q: The Stereo: I bumped the battery with the red "!" and now I am stuck.
hints.a: A dead battery starts when you bump it, and it never stops. That one feeds the wire in front of the gate. Use the switch at the top instead: its wire stays inside the housing.

hints.q: The Night-Light: The corridor is wired end to end, and the current never stops!
hints.a: It does stop, for a moment: a 555 is high a little longer than it is low. Watch the red LED. When it goes out, the last spark races off down the wire: roll in right behind it and keep rolling. Duck into a nook to wait for the next one.

hints.q: The Garage Door Opener: The battery will not stop, and its wire is in my way.
hints.a: Start the battery, and wait for the gate to open. Then bump the fuse next to the battery: it blows and the wire goes dead for good. Blow it too early and the gate never opens.

hints.q: The Wet-Dry Vac: Once I roll over the arrow I can never get back to the battery.
hints.a: Start the battery first, then roll over the arrow. The fuse is on the far side: blow it once the gate has opened, and the wire in front of the gate goes dead.

hints.q: The Power Drill: The red wire runs into a box marked NO. What is that?
hints.a: It is a relay, Normally Open: red current can not get through until pink control current hits it. Then it stays thrown. Turn on the switch on the pink wire, wait, then head for the gate.

hints.q: The Lawn Mower: Once I am past the arrows I can not turn the red wire off again.
hints.a: The box marked NC is a relay, Normally Closed: red current runs through it until pink control current hits it, then it opens for good. Turn the red switch on as you roll by (you will not get another chance), then use the pink switch to cut the red wire in front of the gate.

hints.q: The Christmas Lights: Every switch has to be on at once, but then I am fenced in!
hints.a: Switches in a row: current gets as far as the first one that is off. Work so the live wire never fences you in: turn the switch just above you OFF first, cross over and turn the top one on, come back, turn the middle one on again, then the bottom one. When the gate opens, turn the bottom one off and walk around.

hints.q: The CitiCar: I plugged it in and the headlights came on. Now the charging cord is in my way!
hints.a: A charger will not send a single volt until the car answers on the pink pilot wire, and then it does not stop until the car is full. Turn on the pilot, wait for the headlights, then roll around below the charger and pop its breaker (the fuse).

hints.q: The Home Computer: Both pink switches open the gate. Why do I keep getting stuck?
hints.a: Trace the wires through the chip. The left switch lets the TOP red wire through, and that one ends up running right in front of the gate, for good. The right switch lets the BOTTOM red wire through, inside the housing. Use only the right switch (and never both: each one shuts the other path).

hints.q: The Clock Radio: Snooze button, flashing wires, one-way arrows... where do I start?
hints.a: Bump the timer button as you roll over the arrows. It lets the pulses through for a few seconds, long enough to open the gate. Then wait for it to go off, cross, and slip through the flashing wire between pulses.

hints.q: The Electric Train: Two gates, a switch, a dead battery and a fuse. Where do I start?
hints.a: One gate at a time. Switch on the top wire from above, wait for the left gate, switch it off and go through. Then start the dead battery from below, blow its fuse as soon as the top gate has opened, and walk around to the gate.

hints.q: The Breadboard Computer: The clock never stops racing up the hall, and the screen is just a row of boxes.
hints.a: Run it like the real thing: HALT, then STEP. The pink switch at the bottom throws the relay that halts the 555 clock. Then bump the STEP button: one tick of current boots the LCD (READY!) and opens the gate. The hall is dark now.

hints.q: Home Sweet Ohm: I pressed the timer button, but nothing happened!
hints.a: The timer only lets current through if it is already waiting there. First slip across the flashing wire and turn on the switch in the bottom wall, come back, THEN roll over the arrows and press the timer. Wait for the gate, wait for the wire to go dark, and go home.

hints.q: Some say the felt-maker left something behind in the wiring. Where?
hints.a: In the garage. One board's housing isn't quite as solid as it looks.

hints.q: Which board?
hints.a: The Garage Door Opener (board 13). Look along the bottom of its housing for the faint outline of a little access panel.

hints.q: Show me the wiring.
hints.a: On The Garage Door Opener, roll down from the pad, left along the bottom row to the corner, and keep rolling down into the seam. You land in the house's main fuse box. Roll onto the felt egg and press the space bar to pick it up, then roll into the black main switch to get back.

items.title: Wiring poster
items.heading: THE HOME COMPUTER: WIRING DIAGRAM
items.intro: The trickiest chip in the Bitmore house, wire by wire. Two pink control lines throw four relays; only one combination gets current safely to the gate.

panels.caption: Follow each pink wire up through the chip: which relays does it throw?
